item.title: How Miu Miu Beauty used AI to ensure a successful launch
item.description: In a conversation at Shoptalk Luxe, Miu Miu Beauty chief digital officer Tiffany James explained why the brand is embracing AI for efficiencies, but keeping it out of the spotlight, as the brand's Miutine fragrance gains traction.

item.title: Wellness Briefing: Is absorption the new supplement industry frontier? Plus, industry news
item.description: This week, I sat down with the founders of the 3-year-old supplement brand The Absorption Company, which launched a collection of single-nutrient supplements last week. Glossy spoke to Nate Medow and Zeke Bronfman, co-founders of the company alongside married celebrity couple Nikki Reedand Ian Somerhalder, about the challenges facing new supplement brands today and the details of last week’s sell-out launch strategy.

item.title: The new wave of protein is for the girls
item.description: An onslaught of protein products and the rise of “protein maxing” led some to question if we hit peak protein in 2025. But brands like David and Starbucks are pushing the macronutrient beyond a gym bro supplement and into a building block of an aspirational lifestyle — one that includes matcha lattes and toned Pilates arms.

item.title: Fashion Briefing: Why the new India-EU trade deal will ‘undoubtedly’ have big benefits for the fashion industry
item.description: This week, we take a look at a historic new trade deal between the E.U. and India, one of several major deals being signed between nations and regions without the involvement of the U.S.

item.title: As AI catches on across luxury, brands double down on emotional value
item.description: From Harrods to Amouage, luxury brands are rethinking ROI and prioritizing emotional resonance as AI scales, based on insights from Shoptalk Luxe in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: AS Beauty CEO Joey Shamah on shuttering CoverFX and Mally Beauty (for now), plus warning signs a brand is going under
item.description: Joey Shamah, E.l.f. Beauty founder and former CEO, joined the Glossy Beauty Podcast to discuss his decision to close CoverFX and Mally Beauty from his new role as CEO and founder of AS Beauty. Shamah also shared insights into the challenges of running an underperforming brand, the warning signs that a brand is in distress, and the way an operator comes to the decision to sell, shutter or file bankruptcy.

item.title: Unpacked: Why brands and retailers like Sephora and Adidas are merging loyalty and promotions
item.description: Discover why brands are adopting a unified incentives marketing strategy to boost loyalty, reduce discounting and drive long-term growth.

item.title: Glossy Podcast: Wholesale overhauls, AI strategies and more hot topics from Shoptalk Luxe in Abu Dhabi
item.description: This week, international reporter Zofia Zwieglinska is reporting from Abu Dhabi, where Shoptalk Luxe is bringing together luxury brands from around the world. In between reporting stories from the event, she stopped by the Glossy Podcast to share some of the business themes and trends she's hearing from the executives in attendance.

item.title: Luxury Briefing: Inside LMVH’s ‘quiet opulence’ jewelry brand, as jewelry outpaces luxury
item.description: For this week's Luxury Briefing, Glossy spoke to Repossi CEO Anne de Vergeron at Shoptalk Luxe in Abu Dhabi about the brand's design- and art-led growth. Also, a look behind the scenes at what is working for luxury brands in creator marketing. Plus, executive moves at On Holding, news to know about Alexander McQueen and Saks Off Fifth, and a new podcast episode on the 2016 trend.

item.title: As TikTok embraces ‘Chinese Baddie’ culture, TCM brands see a breakthrough moment
item.description: On TikTok, everyone is suddenly Chinese. It is a rare trend that is overwhelmingly positive. Across race and cultural backgrounds, users have been logging onto the app to document themselves boiling apples to drink in hot water, buying house slippers to avoid walking barefoot at home and ditching cold foods for breakfast. Phrases associated with the trend include being a “Chinese baddie” or being in a very “Chinese time in [one's] life.”
